Alex — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps while this is fresh: 

Recap:
- Primary use case: clinical triage assistant that must return sub-500ms responses for short prompts and batch reranking for longer context lookups.
- Priority features: SDK setup & auth, region routing (US East primary, EU fallback), cost-sensitive routing with latency SLOs, embeddings + reranker pipeline to prioritize clinical notes.

Open questions we flagged:
- How strict are your latency SLAs for synchronous flows vs background/higher-latency rerank?
- Which GCP/AWS regions are your deployments in? Any mandated data residency?
- Existing auth mechanism for 3rd-party APIs (service accounts, SSO, mTLS)?

Proposed next steps:
1) I'll loop in Dev to provide an SDK/auth quickstart and a skeleton routing policy.
2) Send over our model routing playbook + a sample routing config (attached).
3) 30-min technical follow-up next week with your infra/DevSec to validate region routing and fallback behavior.

I've attached the Redwood model routing playbook and a simple test plan template to capture SLA targets — please add notes and share with your infra team.

Thanks —

Thanks Marissa — solid recap. A few clarifying Qs before we bring infra in: 

1) SDK & auth: Do you support service-account style API keys scoped per environment? We prefer short-lived credentials or mTLS where possible.
2) Embeddings/reranker: Can we run embeddings in-region (EU) and do reranking in US if needed, without leaving PII?
3) Fallbacks: If the low-latency variant is busy, we want an automatic fallback to a cheaper model but only when latency is within a hard cap. Is that configurable per route?

Alex — great questions; looping Dev and Rishi for the technical detail. High level answers below: 

1) SDK/Auth: Yes — our SDK supports API keys scoped to project/environment and short-lived tokens via our token-exchange endpoint. We also support mTLS for Private deployments and can integrate with your existing KMS for key rotations. Dev, I'll let you drop an example.

2) Embeddings/reranker: You can pin embeddings to a region (e.g., eu-west1) and run rerankers either in-region or in another region. For PII-sensitive data we recommend keeping embeddings and reranking in the same region — otherwise you should redact or pseudonymize. We can set route-level data residency constraints.

3) Fallbacks/config: Yes — routing is policy-driven. You can set ordered fallback chains by latency buckets, cost thresholds, and model compatibility. Policies can be route-specific and include per-customer overrides.

Next: Dev will share a short SDK auth snippet and a sample routing policy you can review. Once you're happy, let's lock a 30-min slot next Tue/Wed.

Cheers,
Marissa

Alex — hi, quick technical note with concrete examples you can share with Priya.

SDK auth example (node):

// exchange service account for short-lived token
await fetch('https://auth.redwoodinference.com/token', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ service_account_key: process.env.SVC_KEY })
})
.then(r => r.json())
.then(token => {
  // pass token to SDK
  const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: token.access_token, region: 'us-east-1' });
});

Routing policy example (pseudo-yaml):

route: clinical-triage-sync
priority: latency
policies:
  - name: low-latency
    models: [gpt-med-fast-v1]
    max_latency_ms: 500
    cost_threshold_usd_per_1k: 10
  - name: fallback-cost-saving
    models: [gpt-med-balanced-v1]
    max_latency_ms: 800
    cost_threshold_usd_per_1k: 2
region_constraints:
  primary: us-east-1
  fallback: eu-west-1
data_residency: us-east-1

Notes:
- You can set hard caps (reject if latency > X) or soft caps (prefer below X but fallback allowed).
- For embeddings + rerankers: keep the embedding store in eu-west-1 and run the reranker colocated if PII is present. If not, you can route embeddings to eu and rerank in us with a cached snapshot.
- We can instrument per-route tracing so you can see token-level latency and cost; those metrics are surfaced in Redwood Console.

I've attached the playbook (same as Marissa attached) and a sample test plan. Happy to jump on a call Wed morning PT to walk through the routing policy and run a quick spike.
